correctness.rationale: For 3×3 matrices, rational canonical form gives scalar, cyclic, or scalar plus rank one. The scalar shift in the last case is unique by the rank inequality. For C(N) with rank N=1, the nonzero-trace form splits as M2(k)⊕k. The trace-zero form N=E12 gives the displayed five-parameter algebra, and its commutator matrix on the three noncentral coordinates has determinant zero and a nonzero square minor off the center. This gives common centralizer dimensions 3, 5, 9 in all characteristics. Trace duality for the linearized commutator gives tangent dimension 9+d; the underlying dimension 12 at geometric points makes d=3 smooth for the equation scheme. The reduced nonsmooth support is parametrized by scalar translations and nonzero decomposable 2×3×3 tensors, with scalar pairs as limits. The rank-one minor on the open set where suitable off-diagonal entries are nonzero recovers the scalar shifts rationally; this confirms birationality, dimension 8, and irreducibility, not a scheme structure assertion. The projective rank-one directions count L, giving U and the noncyclic single-matrix count S; summing partner counts gives T. Every smooth fiber has q^24 lifts. At (N,0) the trace obstruction for A1 at fixed B1∈C(N) has rank dim[B1,C(N)], 0 or 2, and any admissible first-order pair has q^14 completions. Scalar-base lifts are Tq^18 per pair. These give the stated formula. An independent bit-matrix enumeration over F2 gives strata (6864,588,4), T=7456, and for both E11 and E12 exactly 4 choices of B1 with 512 admissible A1 and 28 choices with 128 admissible A1. It gives J2(2)=177234509824. The frozen VERIFICATION.md and verify_jet3.py were inspected, not executed; their other-field tests are bounded recorded corroboration.

evidence: At the normalized nonscalar base (N,0), write B=tB′, so [A,B]=0 mod t³ iff [A mod t²,B′]=0 mod t². There are q^9 choices of A2. Therefore the fixed-base count is q^9 times the sum of |C(A′)| over length-two lifts A′ of N.

For σ=L (semisimple rank one) or J (nilpotent rank one), Table 2.2 yields Σ_τ a_στ w_τ=(q³+q²−1)w_σ. This follows by substituting the listed group orders: L branches into L,T1,T2,M and J into J,M,N,K0,K∞. Restricting each whole similarity orbit to A′ reducing to the fixed N divides its orbit-weighted sum by the size |O_N|=|GL3(k)|/|σ(k)|. Since dim σ=5 and |GL3(R_2)|=q^9|GL3(k)|, the total is exactly q^23(q³+q²−1), including q=2.

Popov §4.2 already exhibits a rank-two commutator calculation for the subregular sl3 centralizer in characteristic zero. Sharma gives the matrix common-centralizer branches over all finite fields. Their nonscalar d=5 description extends to geometric points by taking finite extensions and is exactly scalar shifts plus a common rank-one direction.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The prior tables cover both the main total and the key exceptional numerical fiber rather than just supplying vague ingredients. The rank-two obstruction is a direct trace-dual expression of the known centralizer branches. Smooth and scalar fibers are standard formal lifting and field centralizer counting. The tangent-locus description follows from the known base cases and the trace pairing. The Segre birational presentation is a useful parametrization of that same stratum, not a separate substantive exact finding here.

evidence: For R_l=k[t]/t^l, the second-jet count is exactly the count of ordered commuting matrices at l=3. Equivalently, it is Σ_A |C(A)| for the algebra centralizer C(A).

Define S as the reduction of C(A) mod t. The group shadow is S× (Avni et al. Definition 2.2 and the paragraph before Lemma 2.3). The preimages of all elements of S have the same size, and invertibility is detected mod t. Thus |C(A)|/|C(A)×|=q^dim(S)/|S×|.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Orbit–stabilizer turns the raw pair count into |GL3(R_l)| times a weighted sum over single-matrix similarity classes. The weight is w_σ=q^dim(σ)/|σ(k)| and depends exactly on the known shadows. This step does not equate the point count with an orbit count, and does not require the unit span lemma for q=2.

originality.rationale: The earlier Avni–Klopsch–Onn–Voll shadow and branching tables mechanically determine the ordered all-matrix count at every length, not just invertible commuting pairs or simultaneous-similarity orbits. Their actual tables also mechanically determine the putatively new d=5 per-base count. The same arithmetic written via second-jet obstruction is a different proof, not a distinct exact invariant; the base stratification is covered by earlier centralizer classification. The failure is demonstrated implication, not an unavailable source or a claim of verbatim duplication.
residual_risks: An earlier source may print the identical specialized polynomial; the documented stronger-table implication already establishes coverage, without inferring authorship or priority from an index.

value.rationale: This is a natural arithmetic invariant and the direct proof explains the exceptional lifts well, but both the claimed numerical invariant and the exceptional fiber are elementary weights of known stronger exact tables. The remaining geometric description is a direct repackaging of the known base centralizer types via nondegenerate trace duality and rank-one tensor parametrization. No independently useful new geometric or arithmetic remainder is established: in particular, there is no singular scheme calculation, new higher-order law, or distinct obstruction result beyond the existing centralizer ranks. No repair is warranted for the stated finding.
